case_name: Kripal and Others v State of Uttar Pradesh
respondent:
State of Uttar Pradesh
Supreme Court of India

25 February 1954
Cr.A. Nos. 37 and 77 of 1953
The Judgment was delivered by: JAGANNADHADAS
1.  These two appeals are against a judgment of the High Court of Allahabad dated 8th May, 1953, and arise out of a trial before the Sessions Judge of Muzaffarnagar of the three appellants herein along with ten
facts: The Sessions Judge acquitted ten persons of all charges.
The three appellants were convicted under section 304 (1) and sentenced to five years rigorous imprisonment and a fine of Rs. 100.
The State filed an appeal against the acquittal of the three appellants under section 302, I.P.C.
The two incidents at Milakwala well and Dhakolas resulted in the death of Jiraj and Indraj, respectively.
The prosecution treated both incidents as forming one transaction and placed all 13 accused on joint trial.
The Sessions Judge acquitted ten persons who concerned solely with the incident at Dhakolas.
issues: Whether the two incidents were separate or part of a single transaction?
Whether the appellants acted in self-defence or committed murder?
Whether the prosecution evidence was reliable and sufficient to support the conviction?
petitioner_arguments: The defence argued that there was only one incident at Milakwala well, and the two brothers died as a result of accidental hits from their own group.
The appellants claimed they were acting in self-defence against an aggressive attack by the prosecution party.
respondent_arguments: The prosecution argued that there were two separate incidents, one at each location, and that the appellants committed murder.
The State appealed against the acquittal of the three appellants under section 302, I.P.C.
court_reasoning: The court accepted the prosecution evidence as reliable and sufficient to support the conviction.
The court rejected the defence's argument that there was only one incident at Milakwala well.
holding: The court upheld the convictions of the three appellants under section 304 (1) and sentenced them to five years rigorous imprisonment and a fine of Rs. 100.
The State's appeal against the acquittal of the three appellants under section 302, I.P.C. was allowed.
